comparison: Both evaluate crystallographic work positively (C4, C55, C56, C116, C117, C137). OpenEval focuses on technical details (resolution, phasing methods, PDB codes), while peer reviewers emphasize the difficulty and importance of obtaining structures. Both find the structural work well-supported.

Perfect claim overlap (C5, C74-C81) regarding FAD-dependent activity and cytochrome c reduction. Both evaluations support the findings. OpenEval provides detailed technical analysis of the data, while peer reviewer notes the biochemical analysis is 'well executed and carefully described.'

Perfect claim overlap (C6, C93-C96, C215) on NADPH/NADH substrate specificity. Both find the lack of discrimination between NADPH and NADH well-documented and supported. Peer reviewer notes the careful study of substrate-specificity properties.

Perfect claim overlap (C7, C90-C92, C136, C217) regarding rate-limiting hydride transfer. Both strongly support the conclusion that hydride transfer, not electron transfer through hemes, is rate-limiting. Peer reviewer explicitly endorses this mechanistic insight.

High overlap (C82-C89, C220-C222) on flavin binding studies. OpenEval provides detailed analysis of differential binding between constructs. Peer reviewer accepts the kinetics and substrate-specificity studies as carefully executed, supporting the structural interpretation.

Perfect claim overlap (C8, C100-C113, C218-C219) on F397's gating role. Both strongly support the functional and structural characterization of F397 mutants. Peer reviewer praises the protein chemistry and biochemical analysis as well executed.

Partial overlap (C9, C143-C149, C153, C223) on D-loop interactions with FAD. OpenEval focuses on Y122 and R126 mutagenesis data. Peer reviewer accepts the full-length structure findings despite medium resolution, noting it conveys relevant information.

Perfect claim overlap (C64-C73) on optimization of purification conditions. Both evaluations support the methodological work. OpenEval details the optimization data, while peer reviewer specifically commends the effort and detailed description of purification optimization.

High overlap (C118-C129) on DH domain crystal structures. Both support the structural findings. OpenEval emphasizes resolution and FAD occupancy differences between WT and F397W. Peer reviewer appreciates the crystallography despite protein flexibility challenges.

Partial overlap (C139-C142) on full-length TM architecture. Both accept the 3.6 Å structure. OpenEval details heme positioning and coordination. Peer reviewer notes the structure conveys relevant information despite medium resolution.

Moderate overlap (C10, C154-C157, C169-C170, C224-C225) on extracellular architecture comparisons. Both support the structural comparisons. OpenEval notes functional implications remain speculative. Peer reviewer accepts the comprehensive comparison to previous structures.

Good overlap (C11-C12, C180-C187, C194, C226-C231) on domain rotation analysis. Both strongly support the conclusion that domain rotation does not correlate with activity. Peer reviewer explicitly states this is a key contribution showing domain rotations are unlikely the main regulatory mechanism.

Moderate overlap (C202-C211, C247-C248) on NADPH binding models. Both support the hypothesis that internal DH rearrangement is critical. OpenEval details structural superpositions with FNR and DUOX1. Peer reviewer endorses that NADPH-binding conformation is pivotal to activation.

Low overlap (C13, C57, C200) but both address NOX2 activation mechanism. OpenEval discusses NBD-to-FBD movement model. Peer reviewer supports the conclusion that domain rotations are unlikely the main regulatory element, aligning with the proposed mechanism.

Low overlap (C233-C236) on p67phox regulation mechanism. Both support the model that regulation occurs at hydride transfer rather than NADPH binding. Peer reviewer endorses the NADPH-binding conformation as pivotal to activation.

Minimal overlap (C249) but both address the overall activation model. OpenEval notes the mechanism remains somewhat speculative. Peer reviewer supports the model showing domain rotations are unlikely the main regulatory mechanism.

High overlap (C240-C246) on concurrent CryoEM work validation. Both support the agreement between studies. OpenEval details specific structural validations. Peer reviewer notes the revised version represents a major contribution and accepts how concurrent findings were integrated.

High overlap (C250-C252) on Liu et al. 2024 confirmation. OpenEval marks as UNCERTAIN due to timing. Peer reviewer's support for the activation model aligns with the authors' claim that subsequent work confirmed their hypotheses.
OpenEval evaluates sequence alignment and domain boundary definition (C58-C63) as supported. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these methodological claims.
OpenEval evaluates extensive background claims (C1-C2, C14-C38) as supported standard introduction material. Peer reviewers did not specifically evaluate background/introduction claims.
OpenEval evaluates prior SpNOX characterization claims (C39-C53) as supported by citations. Peer reviewers did not specifically evaluate these literature-based background claims.
